full_judgment: 2. The facts relevant for the purpose of disposal of the Rule are that Jainal Abedin, predecessor of the petitioners, as plaintiff instituted the suit against the opposite-parties 1-10 as defendants for a declaration that the suit property is not vested and non-resident property and the plaintiff acquired title by adverse possession. His ease in short was that Kali Prasanna Das, Borada Chandra Das and Anil Charan Das sold 0.61 decimals of land to Jainal Abedin at a price of Tk. 1,250 and on receipt of Tk.1000 executed a bainapatra on 7th Aswin 1372 B,S with the stipulation that they execute and register a Kabala on receipt of balance consideration money of Tk. 250. Mono Ranjan Das and Bipin Chandra Das sold .44 decimals of land to Jainal Abedin at a price Tk. 992/and on receipt of Tk. 775/- executed a bainapatra on 20th Sravan 1372 BS with the stipulation that they would execute and register the kabala on receipt of the balance consideration money of Tk. 227 Jainal Abedin got khas possession of the land and had been in adverse possession of the same for over 12 years. The vendors left India and did not return. The opposite-party No. II who got lease of the land as enemy property was added as defendant No. 11 in the suit at his instance. Thereafter defendant a Receiver of the suit property and directed him to render account in respect of the suit property and to deposit the income of the suit No. 11 filed an application on 23-8-84 under Order XL, rule 1 read with section 151 of the Civil Procedure Code for appointment of a receiver in respect of the suit property and by an order of even date the learned Munsif allowed the application for appointment of a receiver and appointed the local Chairman as  property, by possessing the same to the Court.
